world_money_map.summary: The picture remains mixed rather than broadly risk-on or risk-off. U.S. banking-system liquidity received a large one-week boost as the Treasury General Account fell by about $101B and reserve balances rose by about $107B, while the Fed's securities portfolio was essentially flat. Treasury still assumes a $950B end-September cash balance versus about $844B on Sep. 9, so a quarter-end cash rebuild can reverse part of that easing. However, a reserve drain is not the same thing as immediate funding stress: SOFR was 3.62% for Sep. 10, inside the 3.50%-3.75% target range, and the Fed's standing repo facility provides an explicit backstop if private repo funding becomes scarce. The correct interpretation is therefore conditional: TGA rebuilding is a liquidity headwind, but it should not become a standalone risk-asset sell signal unless funding-market evidence confirms tightening. Global policy also remains restrictive/divergent, and the Sep. 15-16 FOMC decision is the dominant near-term event risk.
world_money_map.liquidity: SHORT-TERM US EASING; TGA REVERSAL RISK, FUNDING CALM SO FAR

money_flows.title: Treasury cash runoff temporarily released reserves
money_flows.summary: On the Fed's Sep. 9 balance sheet, the Treasury General Account fell by about $101B from the prior Wednesday while reserve balances rose by about $107B. With the Fed securities portfolio nearly unchanged, Treasury cash movements were the dominant observable source of the reserve increase.

money_flows.title: Quarter-end Treasury cash rebuilding can reverse part of that easing
money_flows.summary: Treasury's Aug. 3 financing estimate assumes a $950B end-September cash balance. The Sep. 9 TGA stood near $844B, leaving roughly $106B to rebuild if the target is met. Because ON RRP usage is now only a few billion dollars, there is much less money-fund RRP cash available to absorb a large TGA rebuild than in earlier cycles, so a larger share can pressure bank reserves or other private liquidity sources.
money_flows.invalidation: Treasury materially undershoots its $950B cash target, or offsetting Fed/liability flows replenish reserves.
money_flows.source: U.S. Treasury Aug. 3 borrowing estimate; Fed H.4.1; NY Fed/FRED ON RRP data through Sep. 11

money_flows.title: Funding markets have not yet confirmed reserve scarcity
money_flows.summary: SOFR was 3.62% for Sep. 10, inside the 3.50%-3.75% federal funds target range, while New York Fed standing repo operations remain available at the top of the target range to cap economically significant private-repo pressure. This means the TGA-rebuild thesis is a conditional liquidity risk, not a mechanical funding-crisis call.
money_flows.source: NY Fed/FRED SOFR; New York Fed standing repo framework

money_flows.title: Global policy is not moving in one easing direction
money_flows.direction: CASH / BONDS REPRICE TOWARD HIGHER REQUIRED RETURNS
money_flows.summary: The ECB raised all three key policy rates by 25 bp on Sep. 10 because energy and conflict-related inflation pressure remained elevated. In the U.S., the last FOMC target range was 3.50%-3.75% and the next decision is Sep. 16. This argues against treating the current environment as a synchronized global liquidity boom.
money_flows.source: ECB Sep. 10 policy decision; Federal Reserve July 29 statement and Sep. calendar

opportunities.title: Preserve cash optionality into the Sep. 16 FOMC decision
opportunities.thesis: The current causal signals conflict: short-term reserve liquidity improved sharply, potential TGA rebuilding is a headwind but funding markets have not confirmed stress, inflation remains above target, Treasury yields rose into the meeting, the ECB just tightened, and U.S. policy uncertainty resolves within roughly two days. The expected value of forcing a broad directional macro position before the FOMC is not yet demonstrated.
opportunities.invalidation: A clear pre-meeting dislocation appears with strong asymmetric payoff and independently verified flow support.
opportunities.source: Fed H.4.1, NY Fed/FRED SOFR, BLS CPI/employment, Treasury yields, ECB policy decision

risks.title: TGA rebuild can become a near-term liquidity drain, but stress is conditional
risks.summary: If Treasury rebuilds the TGA toward its $950B quarter-end assumption from roughly $844B, the cash transfer can absorb private liquidity. With ON RRP nearly exhausted, the buffering channel is much smaller than during the 2021-2024 era. But this should not be interpreted as an automatic market sell signal: secured funding remained orderly at the latest validated observation, and the Fed standing repo facility can supply funding if repo pressure rises.
risks.invalidation: The TGA does not rebuild materially, reserve-supplying offsets dominate, or funding markets remain orderly despite the reserve decline.

risks.title: Rates can stay high even if growth remains resilient
risks.summary: August payrolls rose 162k with unemployment at 4.1%, while August CPI was 3.4% y/y and 0.4% m/m. A resilient labor market plus elevated inflation can keep required returns high. On Sep. 11 the Treasury curve showed roughly 4.63% at 2 years and 4.96% at 10 years.
risks.invalidation: Inflation falls faster than expected and policy guidance turns materially more accommodative without a growth shock.

causal_chains.title: Treasury cash drawdown -> reserve injection
causal_chains.summary: TGA falls -> Treasury spends cash held at the Fed -> payments land in private bank deposits -> bank reserve balances rise -> short-term balance-sheet liquidity improves -> risk assets may receive support if the cash is redeployed rather than retained. The Sep. 2-9 data show this mechanism clearly, but it is a liquidity mechanism, not proof of a durable bull regime.

causal_chains.title: Quarter-end TGA rebuild -> reserve drain -> funding stress only if reserve demand binds
causal_chains.summary: Treasury issues/collects more cash than it spends -> TGA rises -> cash leaves bank deposits / money markets -> reserves can fall because ON RRP has little remaining room to absorb the shift -> but market stress requires the supply of usable reserves/intermediation capacity to become scarce relative to demand -> repo rates and their upper percentiles rise -> standing repo usage may increase -> only then does the liquidity drain become a stronger signal of forced deleveraging risk. Latest validated SOFR did not yet show that scarcity condition.
causal_chains.source: Treasury financing estimate + Fed balance-sheet mechanics + NY Fed/FRED SOFR + NY Fed standing repo framework

causal_chains.title: Energy inflation -> policy restraint -> higher discount rates
causal_chains.summary: Middle East / energy pressure -> higher headline inflation and inflation uncertainty -> central banks maintain or raise restrictive rates -> sovereign yields / required returns rise -> long-duration valuations face compression unless earnings or growth expectations compensate. The ECB's Sep. 10 hike is direct current evidence of this chain.
causal_chains.source: ECB Sep. 10 decision; BLS Aug. CPI

discoveries.title: Reserve growth and Fed asset growth are not the same thing
discoveries.summary: A large weekly reserve increase can come from liability-side shifts such as a falling Treasury General Account even when the Fed's securities holdings barely change. Therefore a 'liquidity' model that watches only the size of the Fed asset portfolio can miss economically important short-term injections and drains.

discoveries.title: Near-zero ON RRP changes Treasury-liquidity transmission
discoveries.summary: ON RRP usage was only about $5.3B on Sep. 11. When this buffer is tiny, a future TGA rebuild cannot be absorbed mainly by money funds simply shifting cash out of ON RRP, so the reserve impact of Treasury cash accumulation can be larger than in periods when ON RRP held hundreds of billions or trillions.
discoveries.source: NY Fed source via FRED ON RRP series

discoveries.title: Reserve drain is not the same as funding stress
discoveries.summary: The causal chain needs an additional condition: reserves can fall without producing a funding crisis while the system remains in an ample-reserves regime. SOFR at 3.62% on Sep. 10 remained inside the Fed's 3.50%-3.75% target range, and the standing repo facility is designed to cap private repo pressure. Therefore the correct escalation trigger is TGA/reserve deterioration plus funding-market confirmation, not TGA movement alone.
discoveries.source: NY Fed/FRED SOFR; New York Fed standing repo framework

changes_since_previous: The TGA-rebuild risk has been refined: a reserve drain is a liquidity headwind, but not a mechanical sell signal or proof of funding stress.
Latest validated secured-funding evidence remained orderly: SOFR was 3.62% for Sep. 10, within the Fed's target range.
The standing repo facility has been added as an explicit stabilizing mechanism that must be considered when modeling how reserve scarcity propagates into markets.
No broad asset BUY/SELL thesis is being promoted before the Sep. 16 FOMC decision because causal evidence remains mixed.
unknowns: The Sep. 15-16 FOMC decision and guidance are not known yet and can materially change the rates/liquidity interpretation.
Treasury's $950B end-September cash balance is an assumption, not a guaranteed realized level; the size/timing of the actual rebuild remains uncertain.
It remains unknown how far reserves can fall in the current distribution of bank balance sheets before repo rates show persistent scarcity; aggregate reserve levels alone do not answer this.
The current data establish Treasury-to-reserve transmission, but do not yet prove how strongly that mechanism predicts equities, crypto, gold, credit or the dollar in the present regime.
August PCE data are not scheduled until Sep. 30, so current inflation assessment relies on CPI plus the latest available July PCE data.
research_frontier: After the Sep. 16 FOMC decision, measure the change in the expected policy path and identify which asset classes should gain or lose from the new real-rate regime.
Monitor SOFR, TGCR/BGCR percentiles, standing-repo usage and reserve distribution as Treasury cash rebuilds; determine the actual threshold at which a reserve drain becomes market-relevant scarcity.

Quantify historically how TGA changes affect reserve balances and risk assets specifically in the post-ON-RRP-depletion regime, controlling for Fed asset changes, repo conditions and major macro events.

Build a point-in-time global liquidity composite across the Fed, ECB, BoJ, PBoC, Treasury cash balances, dollar funding and major stablecoin supply rather than relying on a single balance-sheet proxy.
Establish the immutable Money Intelligence forecast ledger before making the first directional forecast that clears the evidence bar.
